verdicts.note: Attacked as overstated: he has served one commission term since the 2022 election (S9), which is not long tenure. But he is the sitting holder of this office, a former Oroville mayor and council member, and holds several board chairs (S1), running against a first-time candidate. Combined executive and legislative office-holding supports the proven-record pole. High confidence is fine for a factual record.

The evidence is genuinely mixed toward pole_a. He pledges to 'fight Olympia against ... excessive taxation' (S1) and lobbied against the millionaire's tax (S6). But he voted to put the county levy lid lift (88 cents to up to $1.15) on the ballot (S2), then said he did not personally support it (S5) and accepted cuts after it failed (S4). -1 at medium captures that.
Two independent sources: the 'lower taxes' platform plank (S1) and active opposition to the lid lift, 'My plan is for that levy to fail' (S5, S6). That meets the bar for -2 at high.

More than $3 million in specific proposed cuts, including 10% pay cuts for commissioners and department heads (S5, S6). She also offers to take a 10% pay cut herself (S5), backs efficiency audits over grants or new revenue (S6), and wants the budget tightened to 'more sustainable levels' with department fees reviewed (S3). That is concrete, repeated pole_a evidence, so -2 at high holds.

No public office (S1). She is a first-time candidate challenging the incumbent (S4). Her background in party, Farm Bureau and Senate-aide roles (S1, S4) makes her a well-connected political insider, not a pure outsider, which keeps this at +1 rather than +2.

Inapplicable evidence. The basis is a call for 'transparent government', efficiency audits and transparency around infrastructure spending, with residents 'paying more and getting less' (S3, S6). Those are budget-accountability points, already counted on spending. The reform axis concerns money and power in politics: PAC money, term limits, dark money, RCV, direct democracy. The dossier records nothing on those. If anything, she ran with the county party's endorsement through its process (S7), which points the other way. The score double-counts spending evidence on an axis it does not fit.
